Failure Cause Details: Shear plane occurred at 3.5 m depth, exceeding the 1.8 m effective root anchoring zone.
Mitigation: Hengchaovanich (1998) specified: Bioengineering cannot supersede deep structural mechanics; slopes with slip circles >1.5–2.0 m require passive soil nailing or rock anchors combined with subsurface horizontal drains, using vetiver strictly for surficial veneer stability.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for deep slope failure without structural anchoring

Failure Cause Details: High-energy overland flow (>3.5 m/s) struck juvenile plants before adequate root anchorage developed.
Mitigation: Truong et al. (2002) recommended: Plants must be established for ≥6 months before exposure to design velocities >2.0 m/s; where early flash flows threaten, anchor rows with pinned high-tensile biodegradable jute/poly netting over hedgerow crowns.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for high-velocity early flow (<6 months establishment)

Failure Cause Details: EC exceeded survival threshold (>16 dS/m) during active germination/transplanting.
Mitigation: Truong (1994) documented: Pre-treat sodic substrates with gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) at 5–10 t/ha to displace exchangeable Na+; harden slips in containerized polybags with gradual saline conditioning before field transplanting into soils exceeding 10 dS/m.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable under extreme hypersaline conditions

Failure Cause Details: Heavy canopy closure (>75% shading) from adjacent multi-tier agroforestry timber trees.
Mitigation: Utomo et al. (2000) concluded: Vetiver is an obligate C4 light-demanding heliophyte requiring minimum 40–50% full sunlight; agroforestry alleys must enforce bi-annual silvicultural canopy pruning and lopping to sustain hedgerow vigor.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable under continuous dense tree canopy shade

Failure Cause Details: Uncontrolled open cattle foraging before the root crown achieved basal tillering and hardening.
Mitigation: Grimshaw (2000) directed: Strict grazing exclusion via temporary thorn fencing or community live hedges is mandatory for the first 9–12 months until crowns heavily tiller; once mature, prune foliage regularly to 30–50 cm to prevent unpalatable woodiness.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in unfenced, heavily grazed communal landscapes

Failure Cause Details: Water piped underneath the grass row through preferential subterranean tunnels.
Mitigation: Ingelmo et al. (2003) advised: Embed non-woven geotextile cutoff diaphragms (≥30 cm vertical depth) directly beneath the planting trench and place rock riprap energy dissipation sills downstream to prevent hydraulic sub-surface piping.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable without companion geotextile or rock aprons

Failure Cause Details: Repetitive ocean swells (>1.2 m wave height) sheared stems and eroded root matrix.
Mitigation: Islam et al. (2013) stated: Vetiver cannot withstand direct breaking ocean waves; bioengineering must be integrated behind frontline structural geotextile revetments, riprap breakwaters, or outer Avicennia marina mangrove wave-attenuation belts.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable on unprotected, high-energy exposed sea dykes

Failure Cause Details: Transplanted slips suffered complete root death during extended drought without initial watering.
Mitigation: Hengchaovanich (1999) recommended: Transplant bare-root slips strictly during onset of steady monsoon rains, or incorporate hydrogel water-retention polymers into backfill combined with ≥8 cm volcanic straw mulching and initial 30-day manual watering.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable without supplemental irrigation during initial 30 days

Failure Cause Details: Over-compacted subsoil (bulk density >1.75 g/cm³) physically stunted downward root penetration.
Mitigation: Tran et al. (2003) instructed: Deep tractor ripping or manual augering to ≥60 cm depth along planting rows is essential to shatter hardpans; backfill planting trenches with loose friable compost-sand mix to direct geotropic vertical tap-root elongation.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for ultra-dense compacted clays without pre-ripping

Failure Cause Details: Substrate pH dropped below 3.0 alongside high bioavailable aluminum/copper concentrations.
Mitigation: van Wyk et al. (2006) established: Substrates below pH 3.5 require agricultural limestone (CaCO3) or dolomite incorporated at 10–15 t/ha to buffer acidity to pH >4.5, paired with diammonium phosphate (DAP) to precipitate and immobilize toxic soluble Al3+.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in hyper-acidic substrates (pH <3.2) without liming

Failure Cause Details: Gulley headcut undercut the hedge row from behind, creating an unsupported cantilever collapse.
Mitigation: Ribeiro et al. (2010) recommended: Grade gulley headwalls to an inclination ≤1:2 (V:H), line the nickpoint with gabion mattresses or loose rock check dams, and place vetiver hedges upstream on contour to divert overland concentrated flow.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable alone for headcuts >1.0 m drop without rock checks

Failure Cause Details: Continuous total plant submersion (>30 consecutive days of fully drowned leaf crowns).
Mitigation: Le & Truong (2004) determined: Ensure planted slip height exceeds anticipated seasonal flood depth (top leaves must remain aerated); otherwise restrict planting to flood zones where complete inundation duration is strictly ≤14 continuous days.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable where flood stage fully submerges crowns >3–4 weeks

Failure Cause Details: Vetiver row spacing on steep slope (>45°) was planted too widely apart (>2.0 m vertical interval).
Mitigation: Jotisankasa et al. (2014) showed: Hedgerow vertical interval (VI) must not exceed 1.0 m on slopes >30°; combine with temporary surface erosion mats (biodegradable jute or curlex) and inter-row groundcover hydroseeding during establishment.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable when row spacing exceeds standard geotechnical limits

Failure Cause Details: Prolonged subsurface frost layer (>4 months ground freeze, winter temps <-15°C) killed crowns.
Mitigation: Xia et al. (2003) observed: Vetiver cannot survive ground frost depths exceeding 10–15 cm; apply thick winter straw mulch (15 cm) over crowns, restrict plantings to south-facing microclimates, or utilize cold-tolerant regional native species north of 35°N.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in cold continental climates with deep ground permafrost/freezing

Failure Cause Details: Heavy subterranean termite invasion (Microtermes spp.) chewed dry lower root crowns.
Mitigation: Lyimo et al. (2008) documented: Dip root slips in systemic insecticide (imidacloprid or chlorpyrifos) or 10% neem oil solution prior to planting; avoid piling dry dead mulch around the immediate basal shoot crown in dry seasons.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in active termite zones without preventive organic/soil treatments

Failure Cause Details: Silt deposition created an impermeable terrace, trapping excess hydrostatic head behind rows.
Mitigation: Ditiro et al. (2012) advised: Drill sub-horizontal perforated PVC collector pipes (weep holes wrapped in filter cloth) directly through terraced sediment wedges behind hedgerows to relieve pore water pressure build-up during heavy storms.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable on slopes without subsurface drains

Failure Cause Details: Cyclic soil desiccation cracking (shrink-swell cycles) mechanically severed fine root hairs.
Mitigation: Thomas (2005) suggested: Apply a 10 cm thick shredded wood mulch to minimize surficial desiccation cycling; mix coarse sand or organic soil amendments into the upper 30 cm planting slit to reduce high soil plasticity index (PI >35).
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in high plasticity index (PI >40) expansive soils without mulching

Failure Cause Details: Combined waterlogging and extreme acidity/salinity (pH 2.8, pyrite-induced oxidation) killed slips.
Mitigation: Sanyal et al. (2011) reported: Plant vetiver strictly on elevated bund ridges above the active pyritic water table layer; incorporate agricultural lime at 5–8 t/ha with high organic compost to buffer pH >4.0 and complex toxic free iron cations.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for unbuffered marine acid sulfate coastal shores

Failure Cause Details: Average ambient temperatures below 10°C drastically arrested growth and metabolic synthesis.
Mitigation: Rodriguez & Diaz (2005) concluded: Vetiver ceases active vegetative elongation at sustained temperatures <12°C; above 2,200 m elevation in tropical highlands, combine or substitute with cold-adapted native tussock grasses (Festuca and Chusquea spp.).
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable at elevations >2,500 m in temperate/cold conditions

Failure Cause Details: Incomplete hedge closure left 20 cm inter-plant gaps, concentrating hydraulic shear and forming gullies.
Mitigation: Ghosh et al. (2009) directed: Enforce rigid planting centers of 10–12 cm maximum along the contour; inspect and infill dead polybag slips within 30–45 days to guarantee a continuous, impenetrable vegetative filter hedge before flood pulses.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable unless installed with zero gap (<10 cm center-to-center)

Failure Cause Details: Pocket gophers (Geomyidae) excavated extensive burrows through the thick root biomass, severing anchors.
Mitigation: Andrade et al. (2008) recommended: Install vertical 12 mm galvanized mesh wire along the trench wall down to 50 cm during planting in endemic rodent zones, alongside localized ecological rodent population management.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in high rodent-density areas without eradication

Failure Cause Details: Debris flow boulders (>0.5 m diameter) sheared the plant crowns and pulled rooted mats outward.
Mitigation: Ndong et al. (2015) stated: Vetiver bioengineering cannot absorb direct coarse boulder impact loads (>30 kN); install upslope concrete tripods, heavy boulder catch nets, or rock-filled wire gabions ahead of bio-revetments.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable as sole protection for high-magnitude debris flows

Failure Cause Details: Sustained root zone EC exceeded physiological regulation mechanisms (>20 dS/m).
Mitigation: Techapinyawat et al. (2006) established: Upper salinity survival ceiling is ~18–20 dS/m; excavate continuous surface interceptor ditches to divert hyper-saline ground runoff and apply rice husk biochar to moderate exchangeable sodium levels.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for extreme hyper-saline inland sumps

Failure Cause Details: Continuous solid limestone bedrock at 0.3 m depth physically blocked vertical tap-like root anchoring.
Mitigation: Liu et al. (2007) advised: On shallow bedrock mantles (<0.5 m), anchor high-tensile steel wire mesh directly into rock faces using grouted dowels, using vetiver planted in pocket-augered holes (≥60 cm) as a green aesthetic surficial facing.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable on solid shallow bedrock lithology (<0.5 m soil mantle)

Failure Cause Details: Invasive climbing weeds (Mikania micrantha) completely overtopped and suffocated the vetiver row.
Mitigation: Greenfield (1989) documented: Hedgerows require scheduled clearing and manual weeding every 4–6 weeks during the first 12–18 months until stems tiller into an impenetrable, self-shaded basal hedge.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable without periodic weeding during the first 24 months

Failure Cause Details: After drip irrigation was cut, hyper-arid heat (>45°C) and mobile sand depth depleted all moisture.
Mitigation: Al-Otaibi et al. (2014) recommended: In hyper-arid desert zones (rainfall <100 mm/yr), establish permanent subsurface drip irrigation lines (depth 15–20 cm) and install dead-frond palm windbreak fences to suppress mobile dune saltation.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in deserts without permanent supplemental irrigation

Failure Cause Details: High residual free cyanide (>5 mg/L) combined with low redox potential degraded vascular roots.
Mitigation: Russell et al. (2004) instructed: Raw gold slimes leachate must undergo pre-oxidation (aeration lagoons or hydrogen peroxide dosing) to reduce free CN- <1.0 mg/L before introducing effluent into vetiver constructed wetlands.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for raw un-oxidized gold processing discharge

Failure Cause Details: Summer water deficit (>4 months zero rain) induced dormancy; early winter storm stripped roots.
Mitigation: Barbera et al. (2009) determined: Align planting strictly in late autumn (October–November) to maximize winter root establishment prior to summer drought; apply polymer hydrogels and provide minimal auxiliary irrigation during year one summer.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable on sunny Mediterranean slopes without initial summer watering

Failure Cause Details: Waterway deepened by bed degradation; canal bed scoured 2 m below the lowest vetiver root level.
Mitigation: Tadesse & Belay (2011) recommended: Construct low-cost stone-pitch or concrete bed sills across the canal floor to arrest downcutting and establish a permanent grade, maintaining the scour line within the active vetiver root zone.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable when stream equilibrium exhibits severe bed degrade

Failure Cause Details: Massive translational planar shear failure at a bedrock slip interface located at 4.2 m depth.
Mitigation: Perez (2012) stated: Geotechnical limit state of vetiver anchoring ceases below 3.0 m; deep slip zones require anchored micropile arrays or retaining walls, with vetiver used exclusively to dissipate runoff and reduce saturated perched water tables.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable alone for slip planes located deeper than 3.0 m

Failure Cause Details: Consecutive sub-zero ground freeze and frost heave lifted unanchored root crowns out of gravel.
Mitigation: Eyles et al. (2001) observed: Plant containerized mature slips with root crowns buried 10 cm below ground level; weight planting lines with coarse gravel ballasting and anchor with biodegradable coconut fibre mats pinned to the subgrade.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in gravelly soils subject to deep seasonal frost heave

Failure Cause Details: Bulk density too low (<1.0 g/cm³); shear strength of surrounding peat was inadequate to anchor roots.
Mitigation: Lau et al. (2016) advised: Amend peat planting trenches with dense mineral subsoil (laterite or quarry sand) to achieve bulk density >1.2 g/cm³, driving split bamboo vertical stakes to provide mechanical anchorage during the first 12 months.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in pure fibric/sapric ombrotrophic peatlands

Failure Cause Details: Prolonged static waterlogging above root crowns with total lack of dissolved water aeration.
Mitigation: Castillo et al. (2018) directed: Install vetiver on floating artificial bio-rafts or construct raised shoreline berms so leaf crowns sit permanently 10–15 cm above mean stagnant water levels; provide solar pond water circulation.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in stagnant, zero-flow permanent deep swamps

Failure Cause Details: Summer dry grass accumulated excessive fuel load; brush fire burned deep into root crowns.
Mitigation: Sadeghi et al. (2015) recommended: Institute mandatory late-spring hedge slashing/pruning down to 20 cm height, clearing all accumulated dry biomass away from the root collar to prevent crown combustive death during peak fire season.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in fire-prone scrublands without regular trimming/slashing

Failure Cause Details: Free cupric ions (Cu²⁺) at active tailings exceeded 150 mg/kg, blocking cellular mitotic division.
Mitigation: Mitchel (2007) reported: Broadcast lime and zeolite clinoptilolite amendments at 10–12 t/ha to raise soil pH >6.5 and complex bioavailable Cu²⁺ ions before establishing vetiver slips.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in un-amended, heavy copper-rich metalliferous spoils

Failure Cause Details: Lacustrine waves created an erosive back-eddy behind boat docks, undermining roots from the landward side.
Mitigation: Okello et al. (2017) advised: Construct timber or bamboo groynes perpendicular to the shoreline to neutralize longshore sediment transport and dampen wake back-eddies before wave trains impact the bio-revetment base.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable without hydrodynamic barrier integration

Failure Cause Details: Flash flood deposited a sudden 0.9 m thick sediment blanket in a single event, burying crowns completely.
Mitigation: Gomez et al. (2019) documented: Maximum sediment burial accretion rate must not exceed 20–30 cm per depositional event; install temporary upstream porous wire silt fences to step sedimentation into survivable stages.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable where sudden unmetered sediment deposition exceeds 0.5 m

Failure Cause Details: Water salinity consistently held above 18 dS/m with high sodicity (SAR >25), destroying soil pores.
Mitigation: Memon et al. (2012) concluded: Combined hyper-saline and high sodium adsorption ratio (SAR) soils require gypsum applications (10 t/ha), installation of subsoil collector tile drains, and initial leaching before planting vetiver.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in combined hyper-saline / hyper-sodic conditions

Failure Cause Details: High subsurface boron concentrations (>15 mg/L) caused progressive marginal necrosis and death.
Mitigation: Oster et al. (2003) noted: Vetiver displays physiological boron toxicity above 10–12 mg/L; in high-boron agricultural return waters, dilute inflow with surface runoff or interplant with boron-tolerant halophytic accumulators (Distichlis spicata).
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in soils with toxic boron levels (>12–15 ppm)

Failure Mode: Deep slump carrying intact root mat
Failure Cause Details: Global geological fault line failure at 6 m depth sloughed the entire hill face, roots included.
Mitigation: Wright et al. (2010) stated: Deep rotational and translational tectonic failure planes (>3 m) are outside the physical mechanical domain of vegetation; structural anchored retaining walls, shear keys, and horizontal weep holes are non-negotiable precursors.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable as sole measure for macro-geotechnical slope instability

Failure Cause Details: Soil electrical conductivity of 22 dS/m and SAR >28 caused rapid ionic toxicity, osmotic water extraction, and complete mortality.
Mitigation: Mumo et al. (2022) documented: Sodic soils exceeding EC >16 dS/m require mandatory chemical leaching with gypsum (8–12 t/ha) and pit replacement with non-saline topsoil backfill before slip establishment.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in un-amended hyper-saline sodic clays (EC >16 dS/m)

Failure Cause Details: Continuous indurated laterite petroferric hardpan at 8 cm depth completely blocked vertical geotropic root elongation.
Mitigation: EIAR (2021) concluded: Mechanical chiseling or rock augering to ≥50 cm depth is mandatory on indurated petroferric horizons; otherwise hedgerows should be diverted to deeper colluvial soil accumulation pockets.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable over shallow petroferric hardpans (<15 cm depth) without mechanical fracturing

Failure Cause Details: Heavy prolonged rainfall triggered saturation liquefaction along a saprolite bedrock boundary at 2.8 m depth below root anchorage.
Mitigation: MININFRA (2020) specified: On steep slopes (>55°), vetiver must be combined with driven soil nails (L ≥ 4 m) and sub-horizontal PVC weepholes to depress pore pressure build-up along lithic interfaces.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable as standalone stabilization on steep slopes with shallow structural slip interfaces

Failure Cause Details: A sudden flash spate flow exceeding 3.2 m/s swept newly planted bare-root slips from the unarmored gulley channel floor.
Mitigation: KARI (2018) recommended: Gulley floors must be secured using upstream dry-stone check dams or porous log weirs to decelerate discharge velocity below 1.2 m/s until vetiver root clusters reach 6 months maturity.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in active gulley floors subject to unbuffered flash discharges (>2.0 m/s)

Failure Cause Details: Extreme moisture accumulation saturated regolith down to 4.5 m, creating a slip plane far beneath the 2.2 m root envelope.
Mitigation: Kitutu et al. (2011) established: Vetiver effectively locks surficial colluvium (top 1.5 m) but cannot restrain deep-seated mass movements; deep French trench drains and bench cut terracing must precede bioengineering.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable alone for deep-seated rotational mudslides (>2.5 m depth)

Failure Cause Details: Extreme dry season desiccation produced ground fissure cracks up to 8 cm wide and 1.2 m deep, mechanically severing fine root systems.
Mitigation: NEMA (2019) instructed: Expansive vertisols require heavy straw or agro-residue mulching (≥12 cm) along planting rows to maintain volumetric soil water and dampen violent shrinkage-swelling cycles.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in cracking expansive Vertisols without continuous ground surface insulation

Failure Cause Details: Subterranean foraging termites (Macrotermes falciger) consumed dry fibrous stems and basal root crowns during an 8-month drought.
Mitigation: TARI (2020) advised: Treat root slips with biopesticides (Metarhizium anisopliae) or systemic fipronil dip at planting; avoid laying dry straw mulch contiguous with crowns during severe drought spells.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in untreated high-termite hazard areas during extended dry seasons

Failure Cause Details: River backflow submerged hedgerow crowns entirely under 1.5 m of murky stagnant water for 6 continuous weeks.
Mitigation: LVBC (2021) stated: While roots survive submerged flow, foliage must have contact with atmosphere; plant on constructed earthen river levees where flood crest does not submerge crowns for >21 days continuously.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in flood zones where standing water fully drowns leaf crowns >3 weeks

Failure Cause Details: Dense vetiver hedge captured 45 cm of sediment within 6 months, creating a perched impermeable water-retaining shelf that burst during a cloudburst.
Mitigation: UNRA (2022) directed: In areas with high silt delivery rates, back-terrace drainage paths must be cut diagonally to lead water to concrete apron chutes, preventing hydrostatic surcharge behind the living hedge.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable on high-sediment transport slopes without lateral runoff disposal swales

Failure Cause Details: Soil pH exceeded 10.2 accompanied by heavy sodium carbonate/bicarbonate efflorescence, killing root apex cells.
Mitigation: KeNHA (2019) concluded: Vetiver root tissue undergoes caustic necrotic degradation above pH 9.5 and EC >20 dS/m; biological stabilization must be abandoned in favor of basalt riprap or synthetic geomembranes.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in hyper-alkaline trona soils (pH >9.5, EC >20 dS/m)

Failure Cause Details: Extreme aluminum saturation (>75%) coupled with high P-sorption immobilized nutrients, stunting root penetration past 40 cm.
Mitigation: ISABU (2018) recommended: Pre-treat planting trenches with rock phosphate (Minjingu PR) at 200 kg/ha and agricultural lime (2 t/ha) to satisfy fixation capacity and stimulate primary geotropic root expansion.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in un-amended hyper-acidic soils with severe aluminum-induced P-fixation

Failure Cause Details: Severe wind vortex scouring excavated 40 cm of loose sand around the stems, drying out primary root adventitious buds.
Mitigation: NDMA (2020) advised: Establish primary windbreaks using dead Acacia frond checkerboards to dampen surface shear velocity below sand saltation thresholds before planting vetiver hedgerows.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in shifting active dune belts without mechanical micro-windbreak shielding

Failure Cause Details: Canopy closure from dense banana/coffee foliage reduced incident Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) to <25%.
Mitigation: TaCRI (2017) determined: Vetiver hedgerows in agroforestry matrices must be kept free of overhead canopy cover through systematic lateral trimming; hedgerow orientation must be East-West to maximize solar hours.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in continuous dense agroforestry shaded understories (<30% sunlight)

Failure Cause Details: Metastable loose pumice macro-pores collapsed upon sudden wetting, creating subterranean conduits that bypassed hedgerow root zones.
Mitigation: GDC (2021) specified: Pumiceous cut-slopes must undergo mechanical dynamic compaction or surface sealing with cohesive clay veneers prior to establishing bioengineering root reinforcement lines.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in uncompacted collapsible pumiceous soils subject to rapid hydro-piping

Failure Cause Details: Hedgerow planting gaps spaced >25 cm allowed concentrated highway stormwater runoff to breach and carve an erosive chute.
Mitigation: UNRA (2019) instructed: Planting spacing along contour lines must not exceed 10–12 cm slip-to-slip; missed establishments must be replaced within 21 days to form an uninterrupted vegetative barrier.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable where planting spacing leaves unplanted gaps exceeding 15 cm

Failure Cause Details: Transplanted bare-root slips without irrigation during a 3-week mid-season drought spell resulted in 85% plant desiccation.
Mitigation: KALRO (2019) documented: In semi-arid zones, plant strictly using mature container-grown polybag seedlings at the onset of steady rains, or utilize absorbent polyacrylamide hydrogel in planting trenches.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable for bare-root slip planting during unpredictable rainfall windows without watering

Failure Cause Details: Continuous ambient temperatures below 12°C drastically depressed photosynthetic enzymes, preventing deep structural anchoring.
Mitigation: NEMA (2020) concluded: Above 2,200 m altitude in East Africa, vetiver should be replaced or co-planted with cold-tolerant native montane grasses such as Pennisetum clandestinum or Festuca species.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable at high tropical altitudes (>2,200 m) due to low-temperature growth arrest

Failure Cause Details: Semi-diurnal tidal seawater flushing (>16 dS/m salinity) engulfed the root zone, causing rapid hyperosmotic wilting and crown rotting.
Mitigation: CDA (2021) advised: Vetiver must be placed strictly above the spring high-tide level (HAT); intertidal zones must be planted with true halophytic mangroves (Rhizophora mucronata) to absorb salt and surge.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in active intertidal coastal zones exposed to regular marine water flooding

Failure Cause Details: A 4-meter-deep rotational slip occurred behind the 2.4 m deep root curtain following a 3-day continuous torrential downpour.
Mitigation: KeRRA (2022) specified: Vetiver provides upper mantel shearing resistance (≤2 m); road cuts deeper than 3 m in deep Nitisols require bench terracing, lined catchwater interceptor drains, and mechanical retaining cribs.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable as sole stabilization for deep steep-face cuts (>3 m) in saturated montane soils

Failure Cause Details: Local pastoral cattle herds trampled and uprooted juvenile hedgerows to feed on newly emerging green vegetative tillers.
Mitigation: TARI (2021) directed: Community bioengineering works must include binding local grazing pacts or erecting live thorny fencing (Acacia/Euphorbia) to enforce total animal exclusion for at least 12 months.
Exclusion Boundary: Unsuitable in unfenced pastoral migratory corridors during establishment
